title: PSI-Seq
scope: Illumina explanatory schematic captioned "Pseudouridine site identification sequencing (PSI-seq and Ψ-seq)". Inventory of depicted path: poly(A)-selected DNase-treated RNA → CMC/OH− treatment → fragmentation into marked and unmarked RNA fragments → adaptor ligation → reverse transcription → purification → cDNA. The far-left pseudouridine icon is a legend; the three fragments are members of one pool, not separate method branches. No mock-control branch or sequencing operation is drawn. The graph below resolves PSI-seq to Lovejoy et al. (PMID 25353621), explicitly correcting its fragmentation/treatment order with c_order while preserving the diagram observation there. PSI-seq and Ψ-seq are distinct names in the supplied review, not established aliases. Exact transfer of the grouped schematic steps to Ψ-seq remains unresolved. Downstream library conversion and read-start semantics are supplied only to interpret the depicted cDNA endpoint, not to reconstruct an unshown protocol.

Because the library preparation protocol positions a sequencing primer immediately adjacent to the 3′ end of the cDNA, the first base of the sequencing reads should correspond to the last base incorporated by reverse transcription. If the 3′-end of the cDNA results from a stop in reverse transcription at a carbodiimide-modified pseudouridine, the first base of our sequencing read should delineate the base immediately 3′ to a pseudouridine in the mRNA sequence.

states.label: Purified cDNA; PSI-seq interpretation includes selection of truncated inserts
features: The drawn endpoint is three isolated blue strands labelled cDNA, with lengths and selection criteria unspecified.

The PSI-seq primary figure specifies cDNA inserts of 20–80 nt selected from longer RNA templates, enriching RT-stop products. The unmarked-template product remains represented in s_rt_products; recovery of every template-length product is not asserted for the primary-selected pool (c_selection).

The primary paper converts these cDNAs into sequencing libraries using a ribosome-profiling-derived protocol; the card calls this Ribo-Seq/ARTseq. Those downstream internals are outside the drawn endpoint.
After that conversion, the sequencing-read start reports the last base incorporated by RT, ordinarily the RNA base immediately 3′ of the candidate pseudouridine.

operations.label: Fragmentation
operations.description: Shorten prepared RNA into fragments. For the resolved PSI-seq implementation this acts before CMC treatment, as stated in the primary paper; the diagram instead places this block after CMC/OH− treatment (correction c_order).

operations.label: CMC treatment and OH- treatment
operations.description: React RNA with the carbodiimide reagent, then apply alkaline treatment so that CMC is retained on pseudouridine while adducts on uridine and guanosine are removed. For PSI-seq the input is fragmented RNA; the diagram depicts the same block on an intact poly(A) strand before fragmentation.
operations.mechanism: CMCT supplies the CMC moiety; the primary paper identifies the retained adduct on N3 of pseudouridine. The two named treatments form one depicted block.
operations.information_effect: Converts a pre-existing RNA modification into an obstacle to reverse transcription. It does not itself turn RNA into cDNA or separate pseudouridine-bearing molecules from all other RNA.

operations.label: Adaptor ligation
operations.description: Attach a linker-adaptor to the 3′ end of each RNA fragment. Adduct-bearing and unmarked fragments continue together into the adaptor-bearing pool.
operations.mechanism: RNA 3′-end adaptor ligation; no adaptor sequence or ligase identity is specified here.
operations.information_effect: Provides an RT priming site linked to each RNA template, retaining sequence adjacency between the RNA fragment and its adaptor.

evidence.locator: "Adaptor ligation": arrow from fragments to three purple fragments each extended by a green right-end segment; two retain adduct symbols.

evidence.quote: We then ligated a specific adapter oligonucleotide onto the 3′-end of the RNA fragments, to serve as a priming site for reverse transcription.

operations.label: Reverse transcription
operations.description: Extend a primer from the RNA adaptor to make complementary DNA. Extension can stop at a CMC-modified pseudouridine, producing a shorter cDNA; the diagram also retains the cDNA made from an unmarked RNA fragment.
operations.mechanism: The bulky retained CMC adduct is a barrier to reverse transcription through the modified base.
operations.information_effect: RNA sequence is copied into DNA, while the cDNA termination end encodes a candidate RT-stop position. A cDNA product alone is not evidence that a stop was caused by pseudouridine.

operations.label: Purification
operations.description: Recover cDNA from the depicted RNA/cDNA assemblies. The drawing shows isolated blue cDNA strands and does not specify the isolation mechanism. In primary PSI-seq, select truncated cDNA products with inserts of 20–80 nt from longer RNA templates, before the broadly described conversion to sequencing libraries (interpretation c_selection).
operations.mechanism: The paper-supported selection is by cDNA insert length; no unshown RNA-removal chemistry or subsequent library substeps are supplied.
operations.information_effect: Enriches products whose RT stopped within a template. For PSI-seq, the subsequent library places the sequencing primer beside the cDNA 3′ end, so the first read base indicates the last incorporated base, normally immediately 3′ of a candidate Ψ in RNA. Interpretation requires comparison with matched mock-treated material; background and secondary stops limit specificity. The paper reports adjacent stops on either side of Ψ, so exact positioning is an expected signal rather than an invariant for every product.

The supplied 2016 review abstract lists them separately and supports shared CMC labeling, but does not establish Ψ-seq-specific operation order, adaptor strategy or cDNA selection. Transcriptome-wide mapping of pseudouridines: pseudouridine synthases modify specific mRNAs in S. cerevisiae.

In this study, we developed pseudouridine site identification sequencing (PSI-seq), a high-throughput sequencing technique based on the CMCT reverse-transcription stop assay to identify pseudouridines in mRNAs, which we used to systematically characterize the pseudouridine content of the yeast transcriptome.

We first fragmented oligo(dT)-purified poly-adenylated yeast RNA by base hydrolysis, then purified fragments 100 to 300 nucleotides in length. We treated the resulting RNA fragments with CMCT, followed by alkaline treatment to remove CMC from uridines and guanosines, leaving the CMC modification only on pseudouridines.

Size selection for truncated cDNA products with insert lengths of 20-80 nt is performed, yielding only cDNAs whose reverse transcription stopped before the end of the RNA fragment. These cDNAs are converted into sequencing libraries using a protocol adapted from the ribosome profiling technique (Ingolia et al. 2010).
Pseudouridylation meets next-generation sequencing.

corrections.primary_statement: Primary PSI-seq Figure 1D specifies selection of cDNA inserts of 20–80 nt from RNA templates of 100–300 nt, before ribosome-profiling-derived library conversion. Thus op_purification uses this length selection for PSI-seq. The unmarked-fragment product is retained in the inventory and s_rt_products; the diagram does not justify assuming that every template-length product survives the primary selection. Short cDNAs can also reflect background stops, so this selection does not establish pseudouridine identity on its own.

evidence.locator: "Reverse transcription": arrow to three purple/green templates paired with blue strands and magenta right-end segments; the two marked templates show blue extension bounded near the adducts.
"Purification" arrow from RNA/cDNA assemblies to three blue strands labelled "cDNA" at the far right.

evidence.quote: Size selection for truncated cDNA products with insert lengths of 20-80 nt is performed, yielding only cDNAs whose reverse transcription stopped before the end of the RNA fragment. These cDNAs are converted into sequencing libraries using a protocol adapted from the ribosome profiling technique (Ingolia et al. 2010).

We first fragmented oligo(dT)-purified poly-adenylated yeast RNA by base hydrolysis, then purified fragments 100 to 300 nucleotides in length. We treated the resulting RNA fragments with CMCT, followed by alkaline treatment to remove CMC from uridines and guanosines, leaving the CMC modification only on pseudouridines.
In parallel, the same sample is incubated with buffer lacking CMCT (mock treatment) as a negative control.

unknowns.question: Which precise operations, order, adaptor arrangement and cDNA selection apply independently to Ψ-seq? Resolving this requires the Ψ-seq primary method or a full-text comparative account; the supplied grouped drawing and review abstract establish only the family depiction and shared CMC principle.
